awd_abstract_narration:
This award will play a pivotal role in promoting advancing the field of statistics by supporting the participation of graduate students and early-career researchers in the International Chinese Statistical Association (ICSA) 2025 Applied Statistics Symposium, which will be held in Storrs, Connecticut from June 15 to June 18, 2025. With the theme of “Insights into Complexity: Empowering Policy through Statistical Learning and Data Analytics,” the symposium will highlight the role of statistics and data science in addressing modern policy challenges. The symposium aims to bring together a global community to explore how statistical learning and data analytics can address complex decision-making in various disciplines. The symposium will unite researchers, practitioners, and students passionate about advancing statistical methods, biostatistics, data science, artificial intelligence, and their applications in various fields and foster new directions for statistical inference, facilitating discoveries from seemingly messy data to inform real-world impactful decisions.

The ICSA 2025 Applied Statistics Symposium will feature an engaging format, including plenary talks, invited sessions, and contributed posters. We prioritize broadening participation across all aspects of the conference, with a special focus on encouraging the active participation of early-career researchers (those who have earned their doctorates within the past five years) in invited sessions. For students, ICSA 2025 symposium offers numerous opportunities, including a student paper competition and the chance to present posters. The symposium's website, accessible at https://symposium2025.icsa.org/, serves as a hub for seamless communication and resource sharing among participants.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
This award supported the ICSA 2025 Applied Statistics Symposium, organized by the International Chinese Statistical Association (ICSA) and hosted by the Department of Statistics at the University of Connecticut from June 15–18, 2025. The symposium theme was “Insights into Complexity: Empowering Policy through Statistical Learning and Data Analytics.” The conference brought together statisticians, biostatisticians, data scientists, students, and quantitative researchers from academia, industry, and government to exchange new ideas, present recent research, and discuss how statistical learning and data analytics can be used to address complex scientific and societal problems.

The symposium was successfully held with 437 participants from 10 countries. The scientific program included 97 sessions comprising 381 talks and discussions. The program featured three plenary keynote talks, one banquet lecture, invited and special sessions, short courses, student paper sessions, poster presentations, and networking opportunities.

Intellectual Merit

The intellectual merit of the project lies in its contribution to the advancement and dissemination of statistical science, biostatistics, data science, artificial intelligence, and statistical learning. The symposium provided a major forum for researchers to present new methodological developments, compare approaches, and discuss applications of statistical theory and data analytics to real-world problems.

The scientific program covered a broad range of contemporary topics, including biostatistics, artificial intelligence, machine learning, large language models, clinical trials, causal inference, precision medicine, regulatory science, high-dimensional data analysis, survey methodology, time-to-event analysis, dynamic borrowing, healthcare data analytics, and statistical applications in public policy. These topics are central to the development of modern statistics and data science, especially as researchers and practitioners face increasingly complex data structures and growing demand for evidence-based decision-making.

By bringing together participants from universities, pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, government agencies, and other research organizations, the symposium strengthened connections between statistical methodology and applied practice. The exchange of ideas helped promote rigorous and innovative statistical approaches for use in medicine, public health, regulatory science, industry, economics, behavioral sciences, and other data-intensive fields.

Broader Impacts

A major broader impact of the award was its support for students, early-career researchers, and other eligible participants. NSF support helped reduce financial barriers to participation and enabled 41 participants to attend the symposium and engage in scientific and professional development activities. This support expanded access to research presentations, training opportunities, mentoring, networking, and professional interactions.

The project also provided important training opportunities through the short-course program. Courses addressed emerging and high-demand areas, including deep learning and generative artificial intelligence, statistical inference for large language models, dynamic borrowing methods for clinical trials and regulatory submissions, and statistical methods for time-to-event data subject to truncation. These courses helped students, researchers, and practitioners gain methodological, computational, and data science skills relevant to academia, industry, government, healthcare, pharmaceutical development, and regulatory science.

The symposium supported the next generation of statisticians and data scientists through student research activities and awards. The Student Paper Competition attracted 39 submissions and recognized outstanding student research through five ICSA Student Travel Awards, one Jiann-Ping Hsu Pharmaceutical and Regulatory Sciences Student Paper Award, two ASA Biopharmaceutical Section Student Paper Awards, and four Honorable Mentions. The poster session received 24 submissions, including 16 entries in the poster award competition, and four Student Poster Awards were presented. These activities gave students and early-career researchers opportunities to present their work, receive feedback from senior researchers, improve scientific communication skills, and build professional networks.

The project also provided service and professional engagement opportunities for student volunteers from the Department of Statistics at the University of Connecticut. These students gained practical experience supporting a large international scientific meeting and interacted with researchers and practitioners from academia, industry, and government.

Overall, the ICSA 2025 Applied Statistics Symposium advanced statistical knowledge, promoted interdisciplinary collaboration, supported training and professional development, broadened participation in the statistical sciences, and enhanced the visibility of the Department of Statistics at the University of Connecticut as a hub for statistical education, research, and international scientific exchange. The project helped strengthen both the knowledge base and the human resource pipeline needed to apply statistics, data science, and artificial intelligence to important scientific, health, policy, and societal challenges.
